about: The web dialect underneath: react, its runtime

rows.title: Dragonfly for React: a web app in Nuclear — In VS Code: the web device
rows.summary: A web project's toolbar has ▷ Serve, ▭ Device, ◉ Debug, ↻ Reload, Build, Test and Check.
body: A web project's toolbar has ▷ Serve, ▭ Device, ◉ Debug, ↻ Reload, Build, Test and Check. **▭ Device** opens the app
beside the code in a headless browser the editor drives, like the mobile device:
- the size of a desktop, a laptop, a tablet or a phone (with its user agent and touch), rotated or any size
(*Responsive*), at any zoom and always sharp;
- an address bar (back, forward, reload, an address of the app), the page in your browser, Chrome's DevTools of it;
- the color scheme (`prefers-color-scheme`), network throttling (fast 4G, slow 3G, offline), no cache;
- the page's **Console** (a line's source opens the generated file) and **Network** (method, status, address, type,
Saving a `.nuc` rebuilds and Vite updates the page. **◉ Debug** attaches VS Code's JavaScript debugger to the device's
page: a breakpoint in a `.nuc` stops there, the paused line is shown in the `.nuc` (`build/app/.nuclear/lines.json`,
written by every build). F5 with `build/<name>.code-workspace` debugs the app in Chrome instead.

rows.summary: Elements are HTML functions (`div`, `ul`, `li`, `button`, `input`, `img`...) with the attributes as named arguments and `children`; a view is called like a function.
body: Elements are HTML functions (`div`, `ul`, `li`, `button`, `input`, `img`...) with the attributes as named arguments
and `children`; a view is called like a function. `@screen(providers = [...])` creates the managers for the screen;
`CharactersManager.loadPage(2)` inside its views uses the provided one; `CharactersStateBuilder` re-renders on
every state. `goTo(Screen, id = 7)` navigates by screen, never by address.

rows.title: Dragonfly for React: a web app in Nuclear — 5. What is not there yet, and the React ecosystem
rows.summary: This first version has the mobile kinds a browser needs; forms, converters, translations, the local database and the AI kinds come next with the same words.
body: This first version has the mobile kinds a browser needs; forms, converters, translations, the local database and
the AI kinds come next with the same words. ADR-0097 analyses zustand (as the engine of `StateManager`), TanStack
Query (background refetch for a repository method) and react-hook-form + zod (for `form`): the platform's words
stay, the dialect may use those libraries underneath.
The complete example: `examples/examples-web/characters` (built, type-checked and tested by
`tools/react-check/check.sh`). A real site written with it: the NuclearLang website (its screens, managers, search
and content repository are Nuclear; a build script turns the repositories' docs into the JSON it reads).

rows.title: Dragonfly for React: a web app in Nuclear
rows.summary: The web platform is the mobile platform in a browser (ADR-0097): the same kinds and words, so an app's domain, state and tests read the same on a phone and on the web.
body: The web platform is the mobile platform in a browser (ADR-0097): the same kinds and words, so an app's domain,
state and tests read the same on a phone and on the web. The `react` dialect writes React 19 (no JSX), React
Router 7, Vite and Vitest for you. Rules: [web.md](../../spec/web.md) (the platform), [react.md](../../spec/react.md)

rows.title: Dialect `react`: the web platform in TypeScript
rows.summary: What this dialect adds to the platform's sheet: the app is generated as React 19 (no JSX) + React Router 7 + Vite + Vitest in `build/app` (never edit it).
body: What this dialect adds to the platform's sheet: the app is generated as React 19 (no JSX) + React Router 7 + Vite +
Vitest in `build/app` (never edit it). `dragonfly build`, `dragonfly install` (npm), `dragonfly run` (Vite),
`dragonfly test` (Vitest + Testing Library). Full rules: `nuclear help react`.

rows.title: Dialect `react`: the `web` platform in TypeScript with React — 1. Project
rows.summary: A folder with `config.nuc` (`dragonfly(platform = "web", dialect = "react")`) and `main.nuc`; `nuclear build .` writes `build/app`: `src/` (the app; `src/dragonfly.g.ts` and `src/index.ts` generated), `test/`, `index.html`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`.
body: A folder with `config.nuc` (`dragonfly(platform = "web", dialect = "react")`) and `main.nuc`; `nuclear build .`
`npm test` (Vitest), `npm run build` (tsc + Vite). The `[toolchain]` of the dialect gives the `dragonfly` CLI those

| `src/dragonfly.g.ts` | `startDragonfly()`, `dragonflyConfig()`, `registerModels()`, `registerDragonfly()` (configs, the injector, the `@on` subscriptions), `routes` (one `AppRoute` per `@screen`, props from the url parameters), `appRouter()` |
| `src/index.ts` | starts Dragonfly, mounts the `App` of `main.nuc` in `#root` |

| `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `package.json`, `.npmrc` | Vite's entry (title, description, the project's `public/styles.css` and `favicon.svg`), the test environment (jsdom, `test/**/*_test.ts`), TypeScript strict, the dependencies, `install-links=true` (npm copies the runtime instead of linking it, so TypeScript and Vite resolve React from the app) |

rows.title: Dialect `react`: the `web` platform in TypeScript with React — 2. How each kind is written
body: | `stateless Name(params)` | `export function Name(props: NameProps): Element` → `createElement(NameView, props)`; `NameProps` interface (`key?` added); `NameView = statelessOf(class extends StatelessView<NameProps> { build() })`; params read as `this.props.x`; with `@screen(providers)` the function wraps the view in `Providers` |

| `stateful Name(params)` + fields | the same over `statefulOf(class extends StatefulView<NameProps>)`: fields are class fields (`x: T \| null = null` when optional), `setState`, `initState`, `dispose` |
| model | `class` with `readonly` fields, `constructor(init: {...})`, `static fromJson(json: Json)`, `toJson()`, `copyWith()`; a generic model's `fromJson(json, fromJsonT)` |

| `@repository(path)` | `class extends Repository` with `super({ path })`; a `Result` method `return this.result(() => this.send(HttpMethod.get, ':id', { params: { id }, decode: Decode.one(Model.fromJson) }), (e) => new Error({ message: e.message }))`; another return type `return this.send(...)`; `cache` → `new Cache({ ttl })` + `purgeX()` |

rows.title: Dialect `react`: the `web` platform in TypeScript with React — 2. How each kind is written
body: | `usecase`, `service`, `aggregate`, `component` | `class` with `constructor(private readonly dep: Dep)`; `@requires` → `Guards.check({...})` + `return Err(...)`; `@acl` → `await Guards.verify({...})` |

| state model `Name(a: A, flag: boolean)` | `enum NameStatus`, `class Name` (`status`, optional data fields, `static initial()`, `static a(a)`, `static flag()`), `interface NameBuilders`, `function NameBuilder(builders)` → a component that reads `useStateOf(Name)` and calls the builder of the current status |

| `@stateModel(S) statemanager` | `class extends StateManager<S>`; `@state(S.x)` methods become `async x(...): Promise<void>` that `emit` (`result.match(S.error, S.x)` for a `Result`) around a private `_x` with the body; `@before`/`@after` call the named method |

rows.title: Dialect `react`: the `web` platform in TypeScript with React — 2. How each kind is written

rows.title: Dialect `react`: the `web` platform in TypeScript with React — 4. Runtime (`dragonfly-web`)
body: | `Result`, `Ok`, `Err`, `AppError`, `HttpError`, `NotFound` | the platform's Result and errors (`Error(message)` in Nuclear is `new AppError(message)`) |
| `register`, `inject`, `replace`, `resetInjector` | the injector (`{ singleton: false }` for use cases and managers) |
| `Repository` (`send`, `result`, `attempt`, `target`, `purgeCache`), `Decode`, `Cache`, `HttpMethod` | http calls over fetch; GET/PUT/DELETE retry transient failures twice |
| `StatelessView`, `StatefulView`, `statelessOf`, `statefulOf`, `Providers`, `useManager`, `useStateOf`, `useManagerState`, `Element` | views as classes over React components; the provided managers |
| `div`, `span`, `ul`, `li`, `button`, `input`, `img`, `form`... (`el`, `fragment`) | HTML without JSX: `div({ className, children })` or `div(child, child)` |

rows.summary: Dialect `react`: the `web` platform in TypeScript with React
body: > The React dialect of the [web platform](web.md) (ADR-0097), extending [typescript](https://github.com/nuclearlang/nuclear/blob/main/spec/typescript.md). The platform's
> rules, kinds and Nuclear are in `web.md`; this document holds only how this dialect writes them: **React 19**
> without JSX (`createElement` and the runtime's HTML functions), **React Router 7**, **Vite 7** to build and run,
> **Vitest 4** + jsdom + Testing Library to test. Files: `dialects/web/react/`; runtime: `packages/dragonfly-web`
